StaticFindings.Observation: The script prompts on stdin and removes literal U+0020 spaces from the entire input. It does not describe or implement a general byte-stream decoder.
It processes floor(input_length / 4) groups, converts each complete group with int(group, 16), then chr(value); each group therefore maps to one Python Unicode code point.
One to three remaining characters are silently ignored because the loop count is computed from complete four-character groups only.
An invalid complete group raises ValueError from int(..., 16); the source has no exception handler for that input.
The source imports no modules and uses stdin/stdout only; static review found no file, database, registry or network access.
The fixed four-digit grouping does not implement surrogate-pair composition. Surrogate code points and terminal/display behavior were not executed or verified.

RequiredFollowUp: Keep the package unsupported until disposable managed-file lifecycle acceptance passes on the declared Windows target.
Any future runtime/function tests must use synthetic input only and distinguish code-point conversion from UTF-8 byte decoding.
Verify invalid groups, incomplete suffixes, control/surrogate code points and console encoding without testing against user files.

EstimatedRemainingWork.EstimateReason: Static behavior clarification closes no runtime, file-lifecycle or whole legacy outcome.
